source_span: the broader issue is whether the cost and availability of capital become prohibitive for lower quality borrowers ... If credit stress broadens, the implications extend well beyond AI to SMEs, consumers and the broader economy.
source_chain: Sovereign deficits and AI financing needs through 2028 are competing for the same capital, pushing CCC/HY spreads wider, therefore the cost and availability of capital (not underlying AI demand) becomes the binding constraint on whether that demand gets delivered as spending, therefore the real risk is an air pocket in orders for the semi supply chain if financing can't keep up with demand; invalidation: the widening is idiosyncratic (legacy media/cable/building products) and stays contained in CCC rather than migrating into BB/single-B, leveraged loans and primary issuance — if it broadens, implications extend beyond AI to SMEs, consumers and the broader economy.
pulse_chain: Sovereign deficits and the need to finance AI build-out through 2028 compete for the same pool of money, therefore the binding constraint on AI spending is now the cost and availability of capital rather than demand (Privorotsky), therefore the market selloff concentrates in the most levered/financing-dependent names (NeoClouds, CoreWeave, SOXX); invalidation: if the cost of money keeps rising for the lowest-rated borrowers and the stress broadens, the implications reach small businesses, consumers and the wider economy, not just AI — whereas if BB/single-B spreads stay orderly and semi earnings beats get paid, JPMorgan's dip-buy read is right.
why: The pulse reproduces Privorotsky's exact causal chain (capital scarcity, not demand, is the constraint) and his precise invalidation condition (idiosyncratic CCC distress vs. broadening into BB/single-B with spillover to SMEs/consumers/economy), correctly attributed to Goldman and counterposed against JPMorgan's own tactically-bullish dip-buy view.
